findings: The first mutation pass (460 candidates) left 72 survivors. They exposed three weaknesses of the first test set, none a defect of the code under test: (a) test_the_module_global_image_name_is_restored and the error-path check compared A83.IMAGE before and after a call that sets it to NAT-083's own default name, so they could not fail; they now start from a sentinel name; (b) the refusal tests of make_adt85.derive were not isolated (the 'not pinned' input was refused by the trailing-bytes check as well, the lossy and count checks had no message check): each refusal now has an input that only that check can refuse and a message match; (c) the bounds (25 notable lines, 200 characters, 40 process rows, 10 label lines), the 'block ends at the first non-row line' rule, the 'last exec echo wins' rule, a kernel mark at offset 0, and the command-line wrappers of three modules had no exact test. All closed; the second pass left 2 survivors, each explained in equivalent.json.
decide_stage's `no $ exec line` branch is unreachable through analyze() (chain row 1 needs the exec line); it is tested by calling decide_stage directly.

The stage ladder's S1 needs two process lists from the job. NAT-084's timing (launchd first line 202.39 s, keybag task 203.20 s, kernel start about 198 s, loader_return_after 60 s) leaves about 55 s after the keybag task, so two 10 s job intervals fit if launchd does not stop; this is arithmetic from the NAT-084 log, not a measurement of this image.

rc.nat083 is deliberately unchanged so that the chain rows stay comparable between NAT-084 and NAT-086; /etc/quiet is deliberately absent because it would silence the launchd lines the run reads. The cost is that a launchd that stays alive and prints thousands of lines can push the keybag lines out of the returned window (head 8192 + tail 32768 bytes); the analyser then reports S8 with the gap size instead of a negative.
